COVID: Vaccinating South Africa

By: Julian Sun | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
As the world begins to vaccinate populations against COVID 19, how will South Africa go about it and why are we lagging behind?

Unique Selling Point:
We speak with Minister of Health Dr Zweli Mkhize about South Africa's Covid Vaccine rollout strategy. But their plan is already under fire from a many of South Africa's preeminent scientists who accuse the government of dragging their heels, with South Africa seemingly at the back of the queue, as countries all over the world desperately seek out limited stocks of vaccines.

Summary:
The rapid development of several covid-19 vaccines provides the world a way out of the nightmare of Covid-19. Already several countries around the world have begun to vaccinate their populations. But Covid-19 vaccines are only due to arrive in South Africa in March. Why are we lagging behind the rest of the world?

Health Minister Zweli Mhkize says that the government plans to inoculate 40 million South Africans by the end of the year in a 3-stage process. How will this be achieved and is it enough?

We delve into South Africa's Covid-19 Vaccine roll out strategy.

We also speak with Prof Francois Venter, one of a group of preeminent scientists who've written a scathing open letter critical of the governments plan

Finally we interview first responders who will be first in line to receive the vaccine.

Press Release:


COVID-19: Vaccinating South Africa
The rapid development of several COVID-19 vaccines has provided the world with some hope in the ongoing battle against the deadly virus. India, Israel and the United Kingdom have been quick out the blocks in the race to vaccinate millions of their population but South Africa still doesn’t have a single dose of a safe vaccine and experts are warning that government is dragging its feet. But as the country faces a new, more contagious variant of the coronavirus, the question is: when will South Africans get the vaccine? Carte Blanche investigates.
Producer: Julian Sun | Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli

Script:




LINK 1: As South Africa suffers under the strain of a deadly second wave of COVID-19, the need for a vaccine is greater than ever but as of yet, there are none in the country. When will they arrive and what is the government’s plan to vaccinate South Africa?


V/O: Many countries around the world have already begun to immunize their citizens but South Africa is not one of them.

By the end of 2020, South Africa had only secured enough supply for 10% of the population through the COVAX facility – an international market in which countries can buy vaccines, but this will only arrive in the second quarter of the year.

This led to harsh criticism from concerned scientists like Professor Shabir Madhi.

Prof Madhi on missing the boat

V/O: Prof Francois Venter volunteered for COVID-19 vaccine trials last year.

His optimism has been replaced with disappointment with South Africa’s vaccine rollout strategy.

Francois lays out his concerns about South Africa’s vaccine roll out strategy


V/O: In response to their critics, the department of health held a webinar last week to outline their strategy

Minister Zweli Mkhize announced an ambitious plan to achieve herd immunity in South Africa by vaccinating over 40 million people by the end of the year.

Zweli Mkhize outlines the phased rollout plan

Phase 1: Frontline Health Workers 1.25 million

Phase 2: Essential workers, people in congregate settings, those older than 60 years old, vulnerable people with comorbidities – 16,6 million

Phase 3: adults over the age of 18 – 22,5 million



Shabir Madhi talks about the challenges of the rollout strategy.

V/O: The rollout was conceived with help from the Ministerial Advisory Committee. Although he’s chairman of the MAC, Prof Barry Schoub does not speak on behalf of the government.








V/O: A crucial component of the rollout is to secure enough vaccine supply.

Barry Schoub answers this, he must speak about the bilateral discussions with vaccine manufacturers,








LINK 2: Two of the biggest questions about the vaccine rollout strategy are: How much will it cost to vaccinate South Africa and who will pay for it?

V/O: Government announced that funding will be drawn from government funds, medical aid schemes and the private sector. Ryan Noach is the CEO of Discovery Health.

Ryan Noach talks about the private/public partnership


V/O: On Thursday, it was announced that the government had struck a deal with the Serum Institute of India for 1.5 million doses of the Astra Zeneca vaccine, with the first consignment of 1 million doses due to arrive this month.

Barry Schoub comments on frontline health care workers

V/O: It’s enough to immunize 750 000 health care workers. Dr Roxanne Govender is one of them
V/O: The rollout will start in the next few weeks but the task ahead is enormous: government still needs to procure enough vaccines to immunize a further 57% of the population.

Then there’s the huge logistical task of distributing it. This will require partnerships with the likes of companies like Clicks & Dischem

It is an undertaking we dare not fail at.
